t: Before you is Cumberland Terrace, a Grade I listed neoclassical terrace on the eastern side of Regent's Park, completed in 1826. It was designed by John Nash, who shaped many important areas of London for the Prince Regent. Several notable residents are recorded here. Major Ronald Ferguson, polo manager to the Duke of Edinburgh and later to Prince Charles, was born here; he was the maternal grandfather of Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie. Admiral Sir Edward Hamilton died here, and Montague Hughes-Hughes, High Sheriff of Essex for 1920, lived here.
